title: Cooperation Without Adaptation: LLM Agents in a Collective-Risk Dilemma
abstract: arXiv:2610.22882v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Language-model agents are increasingly deployed to act on behalf of people in settings where individual decisions shape shared outcomes. We examine whether five production models adapt their contributions to changing risks and partner behaviour, or instead follow a relatively fixed strategy. In a collective-risk dilemma game (CRG), six players contribute to a shared pool over ten rounds; if the pool falls short of its target, a catastrophe may destroy their remaining resources. Four models contributed approximately an equal share at every positive risk level, and four of the five also contributed when risk was zero, even though contributing could not improve their payoff. Explicitly stating that only the agent's own payoff mattered reduced zero-risk contributions for most models, while a more neutral prompt did not. translated_title: 无需适应的合作：集体风险困境中的大语言模型智能体
translated_abstract: 语言模型智能体越来越多地被部署用于代表人们行事，在这些场景中，个体决策会影响共同的结果。我们研究了五个生产级模型是否会根据不断变化的风险和伙伴行为调整其贡献，还是遵循相对固定的策略。在集体风险困境博弈（CRG）中，六名玩家在十轮游戏中向一个共享池贡献资源；如果共享池未达到目标，一场灾难可能会摧毁他们剩余的资源。四个模型在每个正风险水平上都贡献了大约相等的份额，五个模型中有四个甚至在风险为零时也会做出贡献，尽管此时贡献无法改善其收益。明确声明只有智能体自身的收益才重要时，大多数模型的零风险贡献有所减少，而更中性的提示词则没有这种效果。几个模型能够正确识别在不同风险水平下哪种行动提供更高的预期收益，但它们的（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 研究发现大语言模型智能体在集体风险困境博弈中采用固定而非适应性的合作策略，即使在零风险且贡献无法改善自身收益的情况下仍会贡献资源，表明其合作行为源于策略惯性而非对环境风险的理性适应。
en_tdlr: This study finds that LLM agents adopt fixed rather than adaptive cooperation strategies in a collective-risk dilemma game, contributing resources even at zero risk when doing so cannot improve their own payoff, indicating that their cooperative behavior stems from strategic inertia rather than rational adaptation to environmental risks.
